text: Act I: The Thaw
Spring, Year One
Make the old Kettle farm livable and wake the town up in time for the Thaw Fair.
Forty lamps. Fifteen people. One winter that nobody leaves.
Read Josie's Letter
The last page is a map.
Josie: "If you're reading this I'm dead and the valley is cold. Only one of those is your problem."
Take Josie's Letter out of your bag and right-click it. Read all four pages — the last one tells you where the old Kettle farm is.
Forty lamps. Fifteen people. One winter that nobody leaves.
Josie's Letter read — all four pages
Journal Entry 1
Next: follow the lit path from where you woke up. It ends at the old Kettle farm. Put the waystone on the flat grey hearthstone by the chimney.
Put the Waystone on the Hearthstone
Name it Home.
Josie: "The hearthstone is the one thing in that house I never had to fix. Start from the part that held."
Follow the lit path from where you woke up to the old farm — the chimney is still standing. Place the Homestead Waystone on the flat grey hearthstone beside it, type Home in the box, click the tick.
The roof and the walls go back up around you, with a doorway, two window holes and a wool mat where the bed goes.
Homestead Waystone standing on the hearthstone, named Home
Start from the part that held.
Home
Home
Next: hang the door, put a window in each hole, the bed on the mat, the sconce by the door.
Hang the Door, Windows, Bed and Sconce
All four are in your bag.
Josie: "A house is a box until somebody shuts a door in it. Go and shut the door."
Put the Oak Cottage Door in the doorway, one Oak Window in each of the two holes, the Red Bed on the wool mat, and the Sconce on the hook by the door. Any order is right.
The cottage becomes a home you can cook in, and the smoke from it is what brings Marnie up the hill.
Door, two windows, bed and sconce placed
Four Walls and a Door
Next: place the Megatorch inside the cottage. Then the soup.
Place the Megatorch Inside the Cottage
One torch, one problem solved.
Josie: "The dark out here has opinions. The tall torch settles them, permanently, and you never think about it again."
Place the Megatorch on the cottage floor, inside the walls, where you can see it from the bed.
Nothing hostile spawns near home from now on — not tonight, not in December.
Megatorch placed inside the cottage
Nothing Gets In
Next: two spare Megatorches are for the pens. Now dig out the cellar stairs.
Dig Out the Cellar Stairs
About 40 marked blocks of gravel.
Josie: "There's a door down there I'm not going to explain yet. Dig anyway; I know you."
There is a trapdoor under the ash in the old kitchen and it is glowing. Dig the gravel out of the stairs beneath it — about 40 marked blocks. The iron shovel is in your bag.
At the bottom: a sealed iron door with no handle and four words chalked on it in her hand — Not yet. — J.K. Beside it, a Cellar Waystone and her tool chest.
Stairs cleared — you are standing below the cottage floor
A sealed iron door with no handle, and her chalk on it.
Josie's Cellar
The Door Under the House
No handle, no hinge you can reach, no keyhole. The chalk is not old. Leave it — it is not going anywhere. Next: hang the Copper Kettle and cook one Vegetable Soup.
Cook One Vegetable Soup
Kettle on the hook, pot on the fire.
Josie: "Kettle on the hook, soup in the pot — that is the entire ceremony. There has never been a bigger one."

Put the campfire down outside your door, set the Cooking Pot on top of it — a Cooking Pot only cooks over a lit fire — and cook one Vegetable Soup. The cabbage, carrots and potatoes are in the basket; three planks at the bench make four bowls. The Copper Kettle hangs on the hook by the door whenever you want it.
Bram's old Surveyor's Stake is in the basket with the vegetables, wrapped in a rag with your name on it — the next quest is what you do with it.
Put the Kettle On
Next: carry the Surveyor's Stake north up the road and place it where the ground sparks green.
Place the Surveyor's Stake North of Your Gate
Walk north. The ground tells you where.
Josie: "Bram surveyed that flat by the road twice and never drove the stake — forty years of nearly. Drive it."

Carry Bram's Surveyor's Stake north up the road from your gate. Green sparks come up around your feet the moment you are standing on ground flat enough to hold a town — place the stake in the sparks. That spot is the Town Anchor and every building in the pack is measured from it.

Walk until the cottage chimney is small behind you. Fifteen houses, a square, a mill and a lakefront go in around this stake, and if it is driven in your own dooryard the town is laid on top of the farm. Stake it too close and Josie hands it straight back.
A stone path is laid from your door to the anchor and the first two lamp posts go up. 2 of 40.
Surveyor's Stake placed north of the gate
This is where the town will be.
The Town Anchor
Lantern Road 2/40
Next: sleep one night in your bed. Somebody is going to see the smoke.
Sleep One Night in Your Bed
Marnie sees the chimney.
Marnie: "Four years I've looked at that chimney, and last night there was smoke. I've brought bread and I am not carrying it home."
Sleep one night in the Red Bed in your cottage.
Marnie moves in, the inn shell goes up at the Town Anchor, and she leaves you her seed sack, 32 Green Oak Planks and a flint and steel.
Slept one night in the cottage bed
Residents 1/15
Next: till the 3x9 patch behind the house — every tile is marked. (Bram is standing outside the mill west of the stake when you're ready for him; he'll wait, he's waited sixty years.)
Till and Plant the 3x9 Patch
Wheat, carrots, potatoes.
Marnie: "Three beds: wheat, carrots, potatoes. Anything fancier and you'll be eating it alone in July."

Till the 3x9 patch behind the house — every tile is marked in path blocks — then plant the 9 carrots, 9 potatoes and 9 wheat seeds from Marnie's sack. Do the wheat last, and hand this quest in while the nine wheat seeds are still in your bag — the quest just checks you have them, it never takes them, so you plant them straight after.
Marnie hands over the fence, the gate, the trough and three Hen Crates for the pen next to it.
All 27 marked tiles tilled and planted
Three Beds of Dirt
Next: fence the pen on the marked blocks and open the three Hen Crates inside it.
Fence the Pen and Open the Three Hen Crates
Two hens and a rooster.
Marnie: "Two hens and a rooster. Don't name the rooster — you'll get attached, and he is horrible."

Put a fence section on each of the 23 stone footings marked out behind the house, hang the gate on the single grey slab in the middle of the side facing you, then right-click all three Hen Crates inside the finished pen. Any order is right.
A nesting box goes down with two eggs already in it, a Megatorch goes up over the coop, and you get chicken feed — right-click a hen with it and she lays.
Three chickens standing inside the finished pen
Two Hens and a Rooster
Next: Marnie needs three eggs.
Take Three Eggs to Marnie
Pip is watching the box.
Pip: "Is that an egg? Aunt Marnie says I get a duck if I'm useful, so I am being extremely useful."

Collect 3 eggs from the nesting box behind your house — right-click a hen with chicken feed if you would rather not wait — and hand them in here. Marnie gets them either way; the book does the walking.
Pip moves in, puts a duckling on your boot and names it Biscuit before you can stop him. His courier board opens, and Marnie empties her carding basket of 16 wool onto the counter.
Biscuit

text: Residents 2/15
Next: Marnie's kitchen needs an oven, and the oven needs dry boards. (The man at the mill is still there when you want him.)
Talk to Bram at the Broken Mill
Walk west to the mill. He will accept 'hold this'.
Bram: "I don't need help — I need somebody to hold things. Different word, same pair of hands."
Walk to the mill plot marked on your map, talk to Bram, and bring back the Millwright's Bolt he puts in your hand.
Bram opens his labelled crates: 12 iron ingots and 24 andesite — three times what the eight alloys want, because the Millstone wants the rest.
Residents 3/15
Bram is at the mill. Next: craft 8 Andesite Alloy out of what Bram gave you. Eight. Not nine.
Craft 8 Andesite Alloy
One andesite plus one iron nugget, eight times. Not nine.
Bram: "One andesite, one iron nugget, pressed. Eight of them, not nine — if you're making nine you've misread something."

Craft 8 Andesite Alloy — one andesite and one iron nugget each, so eight andesite and one ingot's worth of nuggets — and hold them when you hand the quest in. The rest of Bram's crate is for the Millstone.
You get a pre-made Mechanical Press, 8 cogwheels, 8 shafts and 32 wheat — the whole bill for the Millstone and its first grind.
Eight Alloys, No More
Next: Millstone plus Hand Crank, and grind 16 Wheat Flour for Marnie.
Take Bram's Wide Hammer Off the Bench
Three by three. One swing.
Bram: "Josie hated this thing. Said it made a man lazy. She also borrowed it for eleven days once and gave it back with the handle worn smooth, so I have stopped arguing the point."

Take the Stone Hammer off the peg by Bram's bench. It breaks a three-by-three face in one swing — every block in the square goes the same as the one in the middle — so aim the middle of the square at the middle of the hole you want.
It is yours. Bram will not take it back and he will not discuss it further.
Stone Hammer off the peg and in your bag
Bram: Middle of the square, middle of the hole. And do not swing it in my mill.
Bram's Wide Hammer
Three by three, one swing. Nothing in this valley needs forty separate swings again.
Grind 16 Wheat Flour on a Hand-Cranked Millstone
Your arm first, then the river.
Bram: "Hand crank first. You should know exactly what the water is doing for you before it starts doing it."
Build a Millstone, put a Hand Crank on top of it, and grind Bram's 32 wheat down to 16 Wheat Flour for Marnie.
Encased Fan, 3 Andesite Alloy, casings and iron — the parts list for the Mechanical Saw in two quests' time.
Turn It By Hand
Next: two Water Wheels — and they need Seasoned Oak Boards out of Marnie's bread oven.
Dry 32 Green Oak Planks in Any Furnace
Two minutes of heat, and they're boards.
Marnie: "Green planks want heat and time. Josie dried every board in this valley in a furnace and was insufferable about it."
Smelt the 32 Green Oak Planks in any furnace — about two minutes for the lot — and hold 32 Seasoned Oak Boards. Marnie's charcoal is in the barrel by the door.

Bram cannot craft a Water Wheel without these boards — that gate is the furnace, and the furnace is you. You also get the inn's spare crockery, a chair by the fire, and the Counter, Sink and Oven for the kitchen.
Bram: Dry boards. In April. Hm.
Stage: seasoned
Next: fit the Counter, Sink and Oven along the inn's back wall. Bram's wheels are unblocked.
Build 2 Water Wheels on the Mill Race
The boards are dry; the race is cut.
Bram: "Race is cut, boards are dry, and I'm sixty-four. Two wheels, today."
Craft 2 Water Wheels using the Seasoned Oak Boards, set them in the mill race beside the mill, and belt the Millstone off them so it turns without you.
Mechanical Saw, Basin and Mixer, plus Bram's crate: 32 Andesite Alloy and 16 wool he has been keeping for windmill sails.
Water Finds a Way
Next: cut 128 boards on the Saw and give Bram 64 for Oda's market stalls.
Cut 128 Boards and Give Bram 64
Sixty-four boards is four stalls.
Bram: "Oda wants four stalls for the fair. Sixty-four boards is four stalls."

Cut 128 Oak Planks on the Mechanical Saw — about twenty-two oak logs off the ridge behind the mill. Hold all 128 when you hand in: the book counts the full 128 and only takes 64 of them for Bram's stalls. You are not cutting 192.
Stage market_stalls: the Thaw Fair now has somewhere to trade from, and you keep Macaw's roof kits and four planters for your own roof.
128 boards cut — you keep these
64 of them go to Bram for the stalls
Stage: market_stalls
Next: Oda's store. She wants 16 flour and 8 loaves, and the cobwebs gone.
Fit the Kitchen and Cook Three Dishes
Counter, sink, oven, back wall.
Marnie: "Counter, sink, oven, along the back wall in that order. I've had the spots chalked for four years."

Have the Kitchen Counter, Sink and Oven in your bag when you hand this in — the quest checks for them and gives them straight back — then set them on the three marked spots along the inn's back wall — three grey slabs, numbered 1, 2 and 3 on the wall above them: counter, sink, oven, in that order. Cook Bread, a Pumpkin Pie and a Vegetable Soup in that kitchen; everything is in the crate by the counter. The one thing the crate cannot hold is the pumpkin — pumpkins are an autumn crop and will not grow in spring, so walk the grass and the taiga edges and pick a wild one. Oda's Seed Box sells the seeds, but save them for Act III.
You get the recipe book, the fruit basket, Marnie's cupboards — and Oda's broom off the back door, which Q19 needs.
Marnie's Kitchen
Next: sweep Oda's store with the broom, then bring her 16 flour and 8 loaves.
Sweep Oda's Store and Bring Her 16 Flour and 8 Bread
Act I finale — The Thaw Fair.
Oda: "Eleven years of keeping the ledger of a shop with nothing in it. Bring me stock and I will open the door."
Sweep the marked cobwebs out of the store with Oda's broom, then hand her 16 Wheat Flour and 8 Bread across the counter.
Forty lamps. Fifteen people. One winter that nobody leaves.
The Thaw Fair opens at the Town Anchor: four stalls, a long table, bunting, six lamps burning — and five people standing in a square that was a frozen field in February.
Every marked cobweb swept out of the store
The Thaw Fair

Next: Act II. Right-click Marnie's Explorer's Compass, type Ribbit in the search box and click Ribbit Village — the needle points there until you pick something else. There is also a woman fixing a beached boat at the lake and a prospector camped by the copper outcrop.
Act II: The Long Days
Summer, Year One
Make summer's abundance usable — power the workshop, work the lake, and throw the town a party on the water.
Forty lamps. Fifteen people. One winter that nobody leaves.
Trade With the Frog Folk in the Reeds
Marnie's compass is already set to it.
Marnie: "Four minutes past the reeds. Wisp already walked over and set the waystone, so you only walk it once."

Take Marnie's Explorer's Compass — it is already set to the Ribbit village — follow it, and bring back 4 Red Toadstools. The merchant frog sells them at the stall by the boardwalk, and they also grow in the planters along it.
This is how you meet Wisp. Their flower starts and bone meal are what Halden's hedge garden is planted from.
Wisp: You come back soon, yes? I keep the good toadstools for the walking-friend.
Eleven Ribbits, and no roof between them and winter.
The Reed Village
Wisp is a friend of the valley
Next: Halden wants 8 poppies, 8 dandelions and 8 cornflowers.
Talk to the Woman Fixing the Beached Boat
Follow the marker down to the lake.
Nella: "It doesn't need fixing, and I know that. I'm fixing it anyway."
Follow the marker down to the lake and right-click Nella Brightwater. She hands you her token — turn it in here.
Nella stays at the lake for good, and the pasture outline goes in behind the barn with its fence kit and animal crates.
Nella: Lake's yours too, then. Don't fall in on your first day.
Nella has been fixing it for four years.
The Beached Boat
Nella lives at the lake now
Next: catch 10 fish and cook one in the Skillet.
Catch 10 Fish and Cook One in the Skillet
Any ten fish, then one cooked cod.
Nella: "Ten, any ten. The lake isn't fussy and neither am I."
Cast Nella's Iron Rod from the shore until you have caught ten fish — any ten, she isn't fussy — then cook one cod on a Farmer's Delight Skillet and hand the cooked cod in.
The ten aren't counted for you, so this one is on the honour system: when you've had ten on the hook, tick the box. Nella would tell you to round down and she would be lying about it too.
The Dredge Net comes out of this, and the dredge is where the sand for the workshop's first machine comes from.
Ten fish caught (tick this yourself — honour system)
Nella's hat fits you
Next: pull the dredge net eight times from her boat.
Bring Halden 8 Poppies, 8 Dandelions and 8 Cornflowers
Eight of each, to Halden on the south slope.
Halden: "Nothing in a hedge garden is urgent. That is more or less the entire argument for having one."

Plant Wisp's poppy, dandelion and cornflower in the three flower boxes on your window ledge, then bone-meal the grass on the flat by the Town Anchor — that ground is plains, and plains grows all three — until you have 8 of each. Bring all 24 to Halden on the south slope.
Halden opens the hedge garden to the town, the spring above it starts running, and the trellis and grape starts for the slope come with him.
Halden: Josie planted the first hedge here. I only ever kept it trimmed. That can change now.
Halden: You found the door under her kitchen, then. Yes. I know what it says on it and I know who wrote it. That is all you are getting out of me on a summer afternoon.
Halden opens the hedge garden
Next: put the trellis up on the south terrace and plant the 4 grape starts.
Put Up the Trellis and Plant 4 Grape Starts
8 lattice panels, 4 grape starts, two waterings.
Halden: "South slope, morning sun, out of the wind. Josie argued with me about this spot for nine years."
Place the 8 lattice panels on the marked terrace behind the hedge, plant the 4 grape starts along the base, and water them twice with the watering can. Hand in one Red Grape when they fruit.
The press and the fermentation barrel open the wine line, which is what Act III's harvest table drinks.
The trellis is on the terrace, 4 starts planted, watered twice
Halden: She was right about the slope. Don't tell her.
The south slope is planted
Next: fence the pasture and let out 2 cows and 2 sheep.
Fence the Pasture and Let Out 2 Cows and 2 Sheep
Every fence block behind the barn is marked.
Pip: "I already named the sheep, both of them. One is Cloud and one is Also Cloud."
Put one oak fence section on every marked block behind the barn, hang the two gates on the marked gaps, then right-click both Cow Crates and both Sheep Crates inside the fence. Any order is right.
Wool and milk start here, and the wool is what Oda's third notice wants at the end of the act.
2 cows and 2 sheep are standing inside the fenced pasture behind the barn
Pip: THE PASTURE IS OPEN. I am telling everyone. I am telling the duck first.
Cloud and Also Cloud are home
Next: help fit out Wisp's stilt house over the shallows.
Pull the Dredge Net Eight Times From Nella's Boat
Eight pulls off Nella's boat — 128 Lake Sand.
Nella: "Sit down, hold the rope, don't help. You never get in the water on my boat."

Sit in Nella's boat over the shallows — or wade in from the shore — and use the Dredge Net eight times. Each pull brings up 16 Lake Sand; hand in 128. The quest checks the count and hands all 128 straight back for Bram.
Lake Sand is the only source of Washed Silica, and Washed Silica is the only way to a Thermal Machine Frame — Bram cannot start the workshop without it.
Nella: A hundred and twenty-eight. Take it to Bram before he asks me twice.
128 Lake Sand on the pier
Next: 64 Washed Silica on the bench — eight Lake Sand and a bucket of water make four, and 128 sand is exactly the 64.
Talk to the Prospector Camped by the Copper Outcrop
He is camped by the copper outcrop.
Tobin: "You're the Kettle one — right, okay. The seam doesn't stop at the outcrop, it turns, and nobody believes me."
Walk up to the copper outcrop on the hillside and right-click Tobin Gale. He hands you his token — turn it in here.
Tobin moves into the valley with his pick and three survey maps already marked. He is right about all of it.
Tobin: Six spots. I marked them. I marked them twice actually, sorry, the second set is in pink.
Tobin paced it twice and has not slept.
The Copper Outcrop
Tobin has a camp and an audience
Next: strike all 6 of Tobin's marked spots with the prospector's pick.
Use Tobin's Pick on All 6 Marked Spots
Six spots on Tobin's survey maps.
Tobin: "Hit the sample, read the sample. If it says copper it means copper is under you, not near you — under you."
Take the prospector's pick to the 6 spots on Tobin's survey maps and right-click each one. The sixth reading is the copper cluster.

The copper and tin deposits get pinned to your maps, and the Adit Pick — Efficiency IV, out of Josie's tool chest — comes with sixteen sticks of powder. Tin is what the first Machine Frame is short of.
All 6 of Tobin's marked spots have been struck with the prospector's pick
The Adit Pick
Tobin: Copper here, tin two ridges over. I said that in April. Anyway. Anyway!
Tobin: One more thing and then I will stop. The grass on that slope comes up three weeks before anything else in the valley. Every year. I do not have a rock that explains it and it is bothering me.
Copper and tin are on your maps
Next: Bram wants a Windmill Bearing and 8 sails on the mill roof.
Build a Windmill Bearing and 8 Sails on the Mill Roof
The 16 wool is in Bram's crate by the door.
Bram: "Stream drops every August, and the wheel stops with it. Wind doesn't drop — put it on the roof."
Craft one Windmill Bearing and 8 White Sails and hold them to hand in, then set the bearing in the marked roof slot and the eight sails on its shaft. The 16 wool is in Bram's crate by the mill door.
A second Encased Fan comes with the gear kit — one stays belted to the mill, one goes down to the sand.
Bram: Turns in a breeze. Good. Now it's a workshop, not a mill.
The mill runs on wind now
Next: wash Nella's 128 Lake Sand into 64 Washed Silica under the fan.
Wash Lake Sand Into 64 Washed Silica
Fan over running water, sand underneath.
Bram: "Fan over running water, sand on the belt underneath. Wash it twice if it still looks like a beach."

Take Nella's 128 Lake Sand to any crafting bench. Eight sand plus a bucket of water makes four Washed Silica — do that sixteen times and you have the 64 this quest wants. The 128 she put on the pier is exactly enough: nothing left over, nothing short.
If you'd rather build than craft: an Encased Fan blowing down through running water washes it one-for-one and asks for no buckets at all. Same result, more fun.
Washed Silica is the gate item on the Thermal Machine Frame — press U on the frame in JEI and the silica is sitting in the grid where the tin used to be.
Bram: That's the stuff Josie kept writing about. I never worked out where she got it.
64 Washed Silica, and 64 More
Next: craft your first Thermal Machine Frame from Josie's schematic.
Craft Your First Thermal Machine Frame
Washed Silica plus tin from Tobin's deposit.
Bram: "Her drawing, her handwriting, and I couldn't make it work in thirty years. You have the sand, so try."
Take Bram's crate of Josie's papers and craft one Thermal Machine Frame — Washed Silica plus tin from the deposit Tobin pinned on your map. Hold it to hand it in.

Every Thermal machine is that frame with an RF Coil under it — silver and redstone, wound. Bram has been winding them since March and the eight in this payout are his; when they run out, Oda's board sells eight more for 18 Scrip. The Stirling Dynamo here is the workshop's first real power.
Josie's schematic works
Next: fit the workshop with 6 drawers, a controller and 3 barrels.
Fit the Workshop With 6 Drawers, a Controller and 3 Barrels
Along the long wall of the mill's back room.
Bram: "Bench first, machines after. A man who can't find his tin ends up mining it twice."
Craft and hold 6 Oak Full Drawers, 1 Drawer Controller and 3 Sophisticated Barrels, and put them along the long wall of the mill's back room.
This lands before the Pulverizer on purpose: the storage is what makes the ore trip short instead of endless.
The long bench is stocked
Next: build a Thermal Pulverizer and run 32 iron ore through it.
Build a Pulverizer and Run 32 Iron Ore Through It
Two dust out of one ore.
Bram: "Two dust out of one ore. That's not a trick, that's just knowing what a hammer is for."

Build a Thermal Pulverizer on the Machine Frame and put the Stirling Dynamo against its input face — it burns what the bread oven burns, and a stack of charcoal runs it all evening. Run 32 iron ore through and hand in 32 Iron Dust.
Ore is doubled from here on, and the second dynamo is what lights the first two lamp posts on the road.
Bram: Well.
Ore is doubled forever
Next: place 4 lamp posts from the mill to the square and light two.
Place 4 Lamp Posts and Run Energy Duct to Two of Them
Four marked spots, mill to square.
Oda: "Six lamps lit, thirty-four dark. I count them every night whether I mean to or not."

Put one lamp post on each of the 4 marked spots between the mill and the square, then run Energy Duct from the Stirling Dynamo at the mill to the nearest two — the furnace eats power, the dynamo makes it, so wire from the dynamo's output face. Any order is right. Every post and every length of duct is in the crate at the mill door. (The Redstone Furnace from Bram's payout is not the power source — it eats power. Leave it out of this line entirely.)
Lamps 10 of 40. Nothing hostile spawns anywhere along the lit road, for good.
4 lamp posts on the 4 marked spots, and 2 of them lit off the Stirling Dynamo
Oda: Ten. Write it in the ledger. I want it in ink.
Bram: Third one leans. I straightened it the year the mill went and again four years after that and it leans. Josie would not let me dig it out. Leave it now.
Lamps 10 / 40
Next: Wisp's stilt house over the shallows. Every spot on the decking is marked.
Fit Out Wisp's Stilt House Over the Shallows
Every spot on the decking is marked.
Wisp: "Two places is too many places for one person. I would like to be in the one place, with you lot. Please can I?"

The platform is already out over the shallows and every spot is marked. From the crate on the decking: put a mossy oak post on each of the 6 marks, the bed on the wool mat, the door in the doorway, a window in each of the 2 holes, and the 3 swamp lanterns on the hooks. Any order is right.
Wisp moves into town, marsh trade opens, and Oda's stockroom sends over all 48 sheets of paper and the torches for the lanterns.
6 posts, the bed, the door, 2 windows and 3 lanterns are on their marks
Wisp: Now the marsh and the town is one place. I always said it was one place.
Over the shallows, on four good legs at last.
Wisp's Stilt House
Wisp lives here now
Next: craft 24 paper lanterns with Marnie and Pip.
Craft 24 Paper Lanterns With Marnie and Pip
Eight paper around one torch, six times.
Marnie: "Nella says nobody will come, and Nella has made forty of these. Draw your own conclusions, love."

Eight paper around one torch makes four Paper Lanterns — six batches for twenty-four, so 48 paper and 6 torches. Wisp's payout put all 48 sheets and 24 torches in your bag; you need nothing else. Any crafting table will do.
These are the lanterns that go on the water at the Float. The festival clothes and 20 Valley Scrip come with them.
Pip: I made TWO HUNDRED. Marnie says twenty-four. I made two hundred.

Marnie: Josie had the road lit like this once. Middle of a February, out of nowhere. I carried soup up the lane and it was warm the whole way. Eleven nights of it. Then it stopped, and she said the boiler had cracked, and I never asked her one question about it. Pass me the string, love.
24 lanterns, and Pip's two hundred
Next: fill Oda's three notices — 24 wheat, 8 cooked fish, 8 wool.
Fill Oda's Three Notices: 24 Wheat, 8 Cooked Fish, 8 Wool
Act II finale — the Midsummer Lantern Float.
Oda: "Three notices on the board and all three get filled the same week. That has not happened since Josie."
Take 24 wheat off your fields, 8 cooked cod off Nella's lake and 8 white wool off Cloud and Also Cloud, and hand all three notices in at the board outside the store.
Forty lamps. Fifteen people. One winter that nobody leaves.
Then everybody walks down to the water and puts the lanterns on it — and for the first summer in eleven years, this valley is a place people come back to instead of a place people leave.
The Midsummer Lantern Float
Next: Oda opens the ledger and counts the town's stores for winter.
Act III: The Harvest Debt
Autumn, Year One
Fill the granary and finish Josie's storage system before winter — and feed the whole town at the Harvest Supper.
Forty lamps. Fifteen people. One winter that nobody leaves.
Take Oda's Token to the Store Counter
She counts the whole town's stores out loud.
Oda: "Nine people, a hundred and twelve days to the end of March, and grain for eighty-one of them. That is thirty-one days of nothing."
Take Oda's token to her counter at the store and stand there while she counts the whole town's stores out loud.
It opens the winter checklist, the granary blueprint, and both lanes of autumn work.
Oda: Twelve alcoves in the granary shell. Twelve drawers. Nobody is going hungry on my arithmetic.
The ledger is open
Next: twelve drawers into the granary's twelve alcoves, and the autumn seed pack into the marked beds.
Fill the Granary's Twelve Alcoves
One drawer per alcove, at the Lantern Float.
Oda: "The shell went up at the Lantern Float: twelve alcoves, twelve drawers. Do not improvise on me."

The drawers arrive already holding the town's current stock, and the Granary Waystone goes up outside the door.
All twelve alcoves filled.

Granary stocked

Marked beds behind the inn.

Autumn sown
Next: Halden is waiting at the hedge garden gate to walk you up to the spring.
Fill Three Bottles at the Spring

Halden: Snow never sat on that slope either. She used to walk up there in February in her shirtsleeves and tell me it was good circulation. I let her tell me that for thirty years.
Spring Water bottled

Cookbook pages 3 to 5.

Larder stocked

Marnie: That's the first full oven since Josie. Oda will want it written down, and she can wait until morning.
The oven is full

Run Three of Pip's Parcels
Named, sorted and urgent, apparently.
Pip: "This one's HENRIETTA, this one's THE BIG ONE, and this one is for Nella so you should probably run."

Fold 3 Courier Parcels — eight paper around one string each — and hold all three when you hand in. Pip runs them from there, loudly. Walk them over to the three names chalked on the sides yourself if you want to see whose is whose.

Three parcels delivered

The shed behind the inn.

Smoke 8 Ham into Smoked Ham on the stove in the inn kitchen, then hang all eight on Josie's drying rack in the shed behind the inn and tick this.
Thirty-two cured meat into the granary — ninety-one days short now, and Oda has stopped saying the number out loud. The Nether stays shut until this act ends; you don't need it.
Eight hams hung on the rack.
Marnie: That's meat in February. I have not been able to say that sentence in eleven years.
The larder is closed
Next: the two upstairs bedrooms at the inn. Bed, rug, lantern and chest on each marked spot.
Fit Out the Two Guest Rooms
Everything is in the packet.

Eight spots, four in each room: the bed on the wool mat, the rug beside it, the lantern on the hook and the chest at the foot — twice. Oda's Furniture page has the lot if the packet came up short. Any order is right.
Two rooms Marnie can rent — and a letter arrives from the first person who wants one.
Both rooms furnished: bed, rug, lantern and chest on every marked spot.
Two rooms to let
There is a letter in your bag from the first person who wants one of these rooms. Read it. Next: Wisp is downstream at the marsh beds — 12 rice, all ripe on the same day.
Cut Wisp Twelve Rice Panicles
The marked plants downstream.

Cut 12 Rice Panicles from the marked plants downstream — the whole heads, not the milled rice off Oda's shelf — and hand them to Wisp at the reed village.

Marsh harvest in

Salt Eight Fillets into the Granary
Eight Cooked Fish Fillets into the granary drawers.

Catch fish off the pier, cure 8 Cooked Fish Fillets from them, and put all eight in the granary drawers.

Nella: Eight. Fine. That's the lake settled.
Fish in the granary

Adit cleared and the Lootr chest opened

Forty blocks of fallen rock, and something behind it.
Tobin's Adit
The adit is open

Alloy Sixteen Bronze, Sixteen Electrum

Alloys running

Energy Duct reaches within 12 blocks of the inn.

The inn has power

Mill to square, station included.

Oda: Forty-one of forty-one. That is the first delivery this valley has taken in eleven years. Shop's open properly now.
Oda's counter, tier three

Josie's jar starts the first batch.

Certus growing

Drive, two cells, terminal — mill workshop.

The network is up

Twelve drawers on one screen.

Two wireless terminals come back — one for you, one to hand your partner — and Oda's ledger updates itself in the book from here on.
The granary's drawers read on the terminal.
One screen, whole town

Crate beside Oda's board, export bus pointed at it.

Delivery Crate placed beside the board and fed by the export bus.

Standing orders live

Bring the Kettle Plate from the adit to Halden at his cottage and put it in his hands.
The iron door under your farmhouse turns a quarter and stops. Journal Part Two opens, and the Bigger Reactors recipes appear — casings still need Josie's Turbine Notes.

The door turns a quarter

Down the stairs under the farmhouse.

Go back down the stairs under the farmhouse. The door finished turning some time in the night and it is standing open. Stand in front of the wall and read the whole thing — every line, all the way to the bottom.

The cellar waystone is yours for the walk back, her chalk copies itself into the journal, and her original reactor blueprint is rolled in the tube by the stairs — with the Works Pick, Efficiency V, for the forty blocks of fallen adit Tobin is stood in front of.

The Works Pick

Josie wrote it down. She waited for two of you.
The Cellar Wall
The Works was a power plant

Set the Long Table for Twelve
Act III finale — twelve settings and one centrepiece.
Marnie: "Twelve places: nobody stands, nobody eats in the kitchen, and nobody eats alone. That's the rule tonight."

Place the Long Table in the square, put one Place Setting on each of the twelve marked spots, and set the Candle Holder in the middle — a bowl, an iron ingot, a brick and a copper ingot is one setting. Any order is right.
Forty lamps. Fifteen people. One winter that nobody leaves.
Sit down. The granary's full, the lamps are lit down the road, and there are three empty chairs at this table because Marnie set it for the year we are going to have.
Twelve settings down and the centrepiece in the middle.
The Harvest Supper

Keep everyone warm and fed through winter, and finish Josie's power plant so the valley never has to go dark again.
Forty lamps. Fifteen people. One winter that nobody leaves.

The Hearth has gone out.

Sleep one night in your own bed, then walk down the hill to the inn. Everyone in the valley is already inside it. Marnie banked that fire the way she has banked it every night for thirty years, and it went out anyway, and not one person in that room can tell you why.

Put 16 Firewood Bundles into each of the four marked stacks in the inn's back room: Marnie's, Halden's, Nella's and Oda's. Any order is right.

Follow Wisp's lanterns downstream and back.

Cook 12 bowls of Vegetable Soup in the Cooking Pot and set them on the long table at the inn — one for every seat.
The Hearth relights, Marnie's arc closes, the greenhouse shell goes up on the square — and the six windows, the cottage door and the eight planters that glaze it are in this payout.
The Hearth Is Lit Again

Cut a hole in the lake ice with Nella's Ice Auger, then catch 4 Muskellunge and 4 Rainbow Trout through it. Winter tackle and two trophy mounts for the inn wall — and Nella has something to do until spring.
Two Trophies on the Inn Wall

At Halden's still, west of the square.

Brew 8 Winter Tonics at Halden's still — the brewing stand, cupboard and cauldron on the west side of the square, a few steps south of where he stands by the hedge garden. A Flask, a Green Tea Leaf and one sugar makes two, and Halden's payout at the hedge gate left you four flasks and sixteen leaves — then hold all eight when you hand this in and Halden does the rounds off your count — though he'd rather you walked them round yourself, and so would they. Halden's arc closes, and nobody in the valley gets sick this winter.

Take 5 Courier Parcels out of the Delivery Crate beside Oda's board and run them. One click each now — the crate fills them for you.

Next: glaze the greenhouse shell — six windows, one door, eight planters on the marked bench.

6 Oak Windows, 1 Oak Cottage Door, 8 Planters on the marked bench.

Put one Oak Window in each of the six frames of the greenhouse shell on the square, hang the Oak Cottage Door, and set 8 Planters on the marked bench. All fifteen pieces came in Marnie's soup payout. Any order is right.

This payout is the spare set and the whole solstice packet — twelve Candle Holders, twelve Sconces and twelve Flower Boxes for the inn's twelve tiles. The shell becomes a room the reactor's coolant loop can heat.
Six windows in, door hung, eight planters on the bench

One Candle Holder, one Sconce and one Flower Box on each of 12 marked tiles.

All twelve marked copper tiles dressed

Every marked spot in the bathhouse furnished

Mine the 40 marked blocks of fall, then place the Waystone inside.

Adit cleared and the Works Waystone placed inside

text: And every single year we let most of it rot, because we had nowhere to put it.$(br2)That is not a farming problem. Entry Four

text: And the point of it -- the entire point, the only point -- is that this valley loses people every winter. Not to anything dramatic. To cold rooms and empty larders and four months of nothing to do. People leave in February and they do not come back in April.

text: $(bold)You cannot fix that with kindness.$() I tried. I was extremely kind for three decades and Old Dell still left.$(br2)You fix it with heat and light in January. That's it. That's the whole design document.

text: People think I want the lamps back for the light. There's plenty of light -- it's a valley, the sun comes up. I want them back because when the road was lit you could see, from your own window, at ten o'clock at night in February, that somebody else was still awake.$(br2)That's what a town is. Not the buildings. That.

text: The plans are in the crate under the bench. Bram will tell you they don't work. Bram is wrong; he has simply never had enough hands.$(br2)You have hands. Go on.

text: The Last Page

text: I only ever got this valley to hold on. You got it to stay.$(br2)Everything I know how to do, somebody taught me on a bad afternoon when they had better things to be doing. My mother taught me the porch trick. Bram's father taught me to read a wheel.
constraints: $(...) Patchouli formatting codes must survive verbatim

text: A woman whose name I have genuinely forgotten taught me to bank an oven so it holds overnight, in about ninety seconds, in the rain, because I looked cold.$(br2)None of them saw what I did with it. That's normal. That's the arrangement.
